by-step report. The richest signal for \"is this server healthy, and why not.\"\n- [Check OAuth requirement](https://docs.mcpjam.c
om/api-reference/server-diagnostics/check-oauth-requirement.md): Lightweight, no MCP connection: reports whether the server is con
figured to require an OAuth grant.\n- [List tools](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/list-tools.md): Returns the se
rver's tools as a collection page. Each item is the MCP tool definition (`name`, `description`, `inputSchema`, ...).\n- [List prom
pts](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/list-prompts.md): Returns the server's prompts as a collection page.\n- [Lis
t resources](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/list-resources.md): Returns the server's resources as a collection p
age.\n- [Read a resource](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/read-a-resource.md): Reads a single resource by URI and
returns its contents.\n- [List server skills](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/list-server-skills.md): Returns th
e Agent Skills a connected server serves over the MCP skills extension (SEP-2640), including skills it advertises that MCPJam decl
ines to load. Not paginated: the catalog is drained server-side, because duplicate detection spans the whole listing.\n- [Get a se
rver skill](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/get-a-server-skill.md): Fetches one skill by URI and verifies it befo
re returning a byte: the SKILL.md digest against the manifest, the fetched frontmatter against what the listing advertised, and th
e name against the URI. Reaches skills a partial listing never mentioned. When a check fails the response carries a `refusal`…\n-
[Read a server skill's supporting file](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/primitives/read-a-server-skills-supporting-file.md):
Reads one supporting file belonging to a skill, checking its byte length and digest against the skill's own manifest. The manifes
t is the read allowlist and is re-fetched here rather than accepted from the caller, so a request cannot authorize its own read.\n
- [Export a server snapshot](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/export/export-a-server-snapshot.md): Lists tools, resources, an
d prompts in one call and returns a single JSON snapshot — handy for diffing a server's surface over time in CI.\n- [Call a tool](
https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/call-a-tool.md): Executes a tool on the server and returns the MCP `CallToolResult
` plus an additive `durationMs` (wall-clock time of `executeTool`). Tool-level failures (`isError: true` in the result) are **succ
essful calls** — the server answered; only transport/auth errors use the error envelope.\n- [Render a prompt](https://docs.mcpjam.
com/api-reference/execution/render-a-prompt.md): Renders a prompt with arguments and returns the MCP `GetPromptResult` directly (`
description?`, `messages`).\n- [Render an MCP App widget headlessly](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/render-an-mcp
-app-widget-headlessly.md): Call an MCP App tool and mount its `ui://` widget in real headless Chromium running the production hos
t bridge, then report whether it rendered, what it logged, what it was blocked from fetching, and the widget as an accessibility t
ree with addressable elements.\n- [Create a retained widget session](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/create-a-reta
ined-widget-session.md): Available only on the local Inspector that created the session; hosted deployments return 404. Requires a
verified user or API key. A session is bound to the original subject, project and server and expires after its idle timeout. Exec
utes the tool and retains its App in one local Chromium context.…\n- [Read a retained widget snapshot](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api

ires after its idle timeout. Returns an accessibility tree and addressable elements without replay…\n- [Act on a retained widget](

he session; hosted deployments return 404. Requires a verified user or API key. A session is bound to the original subject, projec
t and server and expires after its idle timeout. Runs one coordinate action with fresh project/server authorization.\n- [Run a ret
ained widget step](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/run-a-retained-widget-step.md): Available only on the local Ins
pector that created the session; hosted deployments return 404. Requires a verified user or API key. A session is bound to the ori
ginal subject, project and server and expires after its idle timeout. Runs one semantic action or assertion, using the same locato
r vocabul…\n- [Close a retained widget session](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/execution/close-a-retained-widget-session.md
): Available only on the local Inspector that created the session; hosted deployments return 404. Requires a verified user or API
key. A session is bound to the original subject, project and server and expires after its idle timeout. Disposes the original owne
r's browser. Returns closed=false if no mat…\n- [List a suite's settings history](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-suite
s/list-a-suites-settings-history.md): One entry per committed edit to the suite's settings, newest first: who made it, which STORE
D fields moved, the note they left, how many runs were launched against it, and the revision group that ties one request's writes
together. Rows carry no configuration snapshots. Send a `revisionNumber` back…\n- [Attach one environment to a suite (atomic appen
d)](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-suites/attach-one-environment-to-a-suite-atomic-append.md): APPEND one project envi
ronment to the suite's attachments, if it is not already there.\n- [List a server's accounts](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-referenc
e/server-accounts/list-a-servers-accounts.md): The accounts this server signs in with that you can see: your own personal accounts
, or, on a server shared with the project, its project accounts. Another member's personal account never appears. METADATA ONLY: n
o account response carries a token.\n- [Get a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/get-a-server-a
ccount.md): One account, by id or name. Another member's personal account answers `404`, the same as a missing one. A name two acc
ounts share answers `409` with `details.code: \"account_name_ambiguous\"` and both ids in `details.accountIds`.\n- [Upload tokens
to a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/upload-tokens-to-a-server-account.md): Creates the acco
unt (`201`) or replaces its token in place (`200`, same id). A well-formed account id never creates one: an unknown id is `404`. A
ny other reference is a name, and a name no account has creates the account.\n- [Delete a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/
api-reference/server-accounts/delete-a-server-account.md): Deletes the account and its stored token. The token's issuer is asked t
o revoke it where the issuer supports revocation (best effort), which also invalidates any copy of the same token you hold.\n- [Re
name a server account or make it the default](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/rename-a-server-account-or-mak
e-it-the-default.md): Rename the account, make it the default, or both; a rename applies first. A name another account on the serv
er uses answers `409` with `details.code: \"account_name_taken\"`.\n- [Import OAuth tokens](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/
oauth/import-oauth-tokens.md): **Deprecated.** Use `PUT /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/accounts/{account}`. This route u
ploads to your default account on the server, creating an unnamed one when the server has none, and is removed 90 days after the a
